heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
All inbound requests to the Integration Gateway MUST present a valid cryptographically signed bearer token.
Requests lacking valid credentials SHALL be rejected immediately with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Destructive in-place updates on active requirements, specifications, and topological edges MUST NOT occur.
Every approved state mutation SHALL be recorded as a discrete, reversible event in the audit ledger.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Every active functional specification and implementation task MUST maintain an unbroken upward directed edge path to an active requirement root.
Orphan execution tasks SHALL NOT be permitted in the active graph topology.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Candidate requirements and exploratory agent mutations MUST be stored with lifecycle state DRAFT.
Draft entities SHALL be caller-scoped and isolated from production agent context envelopes until approved.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
All requirement vector embeddings MUST specify fixed dimensionality of 384 dimensions matching the reference model.
Dense vector indexing SHALL utilize partial HNSW cosine distance indexes restricted to completed embeddings.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Any transaction that mutates active graph topology or approves draft batches MUST acquire a global advisory lock.
Lock acquisition SHALL precede any row-level locks to prevent deadlocks across concurrent sessions.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Every requirement derived through the decomposition pipeline MUST store 0-based byte span coordinates.
Span extraction SHALL verify character boundary safety before committing source span offsets.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Permissions to alter or elaborate a graph node MUST be governed by explicit per-node governance policies.
Node policies SHALL take absolute precedence over global agent roles.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Every mutation submitted through the gateway MUST be attributable to a verified identity.
Unauthenticated or anonymous mutations SHALL be rejected at the gateway boundary.

heading: 3. Normative Requirements & Invariants
text:
Micro-reflex graph traversal queries MUST execute in less than 50 milliseconds for up to 3 hops.
Context envelope assembly queries SHALL complete in less than 100 milliseconds.

heading: 3. Architectural Invariants
text: Every active functional specification, implementation task, and code artifact reference must maintain a valid directed edge path terminating at an authorized active requirement node. Entities in DRAFT, NEEDS_REVERIFICATION, SUPERSEDED, or ARCHIVED states are explicitly exempt from requiring active requirement ancestors. Orphan execution tasks must be rejected at the database constraint level.

heading: 3. Architectural Invariants
text: Destructive in-place updates (UPDATE, DELETE) on active requirements, specifications, and topological edges must not occur. Structural edges in graph_edges maintain a strongly typed lifecycle_state (DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, REVERTED) and are never physically deleted.

heading: 3. Architectural Invariants
text: The core database engine and gateway services must never execute autonomous agent cognitive loops internally. The substrate must function strictly as a deterministic state store and protocol gateway.

heading: 3. Architectural Invariants
text: Every requirement derived via the decomposition pipeline must store a persistent cryptographic reference (Git commit/blob hash doc_hash), document path/slug (doc_path), and 0-based source byte span coordinates (byte_start, byte_end) embedded as first-class columns directly on graph_nodes pointing to the original document artifact.

heading: 3. Architectural Invariants
text: Permissions to alter or elaborate a graph node must be governed by explicit per-node governance_policy metadata attributes (AUTONOMOUS_ELABORATION, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, LOCKED). Node-level policies must take absolute precedence over global agent roles.

heading: 3. Architectural Invariants
text: The Knowledge Substrate must be used to manage its own development through a phased bootstrapping transition. Upon completing Phase 1 foundational ingestion and read-only context retrieval, the substrate must self-host its own documentation for context querying.

heading: 3. Architectural Invariants
text: Every mutation and candidate draft submitted through the Integration Gateway must be attributable to a verified external identity (human user or agent instance). All draft rows in graph_nodes and graph_edges must enforce created_by VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL to provide caller-scoped draft isolation via partial indexes.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Pure Rust package repository: all substrate service code is authored in Rust (edition 2024), built via Cargo stable toolchain.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Single PostgreSQL engine: all topology data, vector embeddings (pgvector), relational metadata, and audit records reside in one PostgreSQL instance; no external graph or vector databases.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Stateless gateway boundary: MCP and REST interfaces maintain no persistent session memory; every operation is an authenticated, isolated transaction.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Document immutability & embedded source spans: uploaded text specifications are stored in a Git-backed repository committed to a dedicated specifications branch with mandatory persistent document paths (doc_path).

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: LLM interaction restricted to human-directed document ingestion and decomposition pipelines only.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Dependency policy: prefer well-established Rust crates; avoid dependencies for functionality small enough to implement with the standard library.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Mechanical-first extraction: decomposition must execute CommonMark AST parsing and keyword scanning mechanically; LLMs must never echo verbatim source text and output only compact classification tuples.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Draft lifecycle isolation & staging consolidation: candidate requirements from decomposition and agent proposals reside directly in graph_nodes and graph_edges with lifecycle_state = 'DRAFT' and mandatory created_by VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL attribution.

heading: 2.2 Derived Constraints
text: Strict lock acquisition hierarchy: any transaction that performs structural edge mutations, DAG cycle checks, batch staging approvals, or rollbacks must acquire the global transaction advisory lock before acquiring any row-level locks on graph_nodes or graph_edges.

heading: 1. Executive Summary & Overview
text:
The Knowledge Substrate manages system evolution through governed requirement topologies.
This document outlines technical specifications, operational policies, and implementation tasks.

heading: 2. System Architecture & Topology
text:
The architecture consists of a stateless API gateway, a background worker pool, and a unified PostgreSQL database.
All external interactions flow through standard Model Context Protocol (MCP) and REST endpoints.

heading: 2.1 Database Schema
text:
The database uses PostgreSQL 16+ with the pgvector extension for dense vector similarity search.
All state transitions are recorded in an append-only audit ledger with monotonic sequence numbers.

heading: 4. Implementation Tasks

heading: 4. Implementation Tasks
text:

heading: 4. Implementation Tasks
text:

Measure token consumption ratio ensuring generated output tokens represent less than 10% of document input tokens.

heading: 4. Implementation Tasks
text:
Evaluate local embedding generation using fastembed and all-MiniLM-L6-v2 on commodity CPU hardware.
Measure inference latency across batches of 1, 8, and 32 requirement chunks.

heading: 4. Implementation Tasks

heading: 5. Non-Normative Guidelines & Future Considerations
text:
System operators should periodically inspect database index bloat and vacuum statistics.
Developers are encouraged to author clear, atomic specification blocks to facilitate automated decomposition.
In future iterations, additional embedding models and multi-lingual parsers may be evaluated.

heading: 1. Problem Space & Structural Dilemma
text: The fundamental tension in modern software engineering is that software complexity grows quadratically while human cognitive capacity remains constant. Autonomous agents offer immense speed but create intent drift when decoupled from governing architecture.

heading: 2. Key Capabilities
text: The Knowledge Substrate bridges human architectural intent with autonomous agent execution through five core capabilities: Assisted Extraction, Governed Topology, Micro-Reflex Context Retrieval, Continuous Audit Ledger, and Topological Auditing.

heading: 3. Foundational Metaphor: The Living Blueprint
text: Unlike static requirements documents or ephemeral issue trackers, the substrate models technical systems as an interconnected, living property graph that evolves alongside the codebase.

heading: 4. High-Level Architecture
text: The architecture comprises three core conceptual layers: the Document Ledger, the Governed Graph Store, and the Model Context Protocol Gateway.

heading: 5. Invariants, Boundary Constraints & Hypotheses
text: Hypothesis H-1 (Governed Requirement Topologies vs. Ad-Hoc Agentic Retrieval): We hypothesize that anchoring external agents to a purpose-built, version-governed requirement graph provides decisive advantage over best-available code-level agentic retrieval.

heading: 5. Invariants, Boundary Constraints & Hypotheses
text: Hypothesis H-2 (Sublinear Human Oversight Overhead): We hypothesize that managing autonomous agents through structured requirement graphs significantly reduces human supervisory overhead compared to manual PR code diff inspection.

heading: 5. Invariants, Boundary Constraints & Hypotheses
text: Hypothesis H-3 (Single-Engine Relational Scalability): We hypothesize that a single PostgreSQL instance combining graph query patterns and pgvector scales comfortably to support large-scale enterprise project graphs without dedicated graph clusters.

heading: 5. Invariants, Boundary Constraints & Hypotheses
text: Hypothesis H-4 (Assisted Ingestion Accuracy): We hypothesize that a human-in-the-loop decomposition pipeline powered by commodity LLMs achieves high-fidelity requirement extraction from unstructured technical markdown.

heading: 5. Invariants, Boundary Constraints & Hypotheses
text: Hypothesis H-5 (Topological Gap Detection & Procedural Scaffolding): We hypothesize that structuring institutional procedures as a navigable property graph allows structural traversals to detect systemic gaps significantly earlier than conventional reviews.

heading: 6. Multi-Axis Progression Model
text: Program advancement is organized across two orthogonal vectors: Governance & Provenance Maturity and Agent Autonomy & Integration Breadth.

heading: 7. Anti-Goals & Strategic Boundaries
text: The substrate is not a general-purpose project management system, not an IDE plugin, and not an autonomous software factory.
